sections.topic: Scheduled Tribe definition and criteria
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-4 › Tribe - definition, classification, distribution and characteristics › Scheduled Tribe definition and criteria - Art. 366(25), Art. 342, Lokur criteria
bullets: 'Tribe' comes from Latin 'tribus'; Marshall Sahlins: a segmental organisation of equivalent, unspecialised multi-family groups, clans or bands.
Art. 366(25): STs are communities "deemed under Article 342" to be STs. The term took shape under the GoI Act 1935 and the Constitution.

Art. 342(1): President notifies, after consulting the Governor (first order: Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950); Art. 342(2): only Parliament by law can include or exclude. Lists are state/UT-specific.

Criteria (not in the Constitution): primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact with the community at large, backwardness (BPSC 2023: all four). Drawn from Census 1931, Kalelkar (1955), Lokur Committee (1965) and Chanda Committee (1969) (IYB 2026).
